function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here are some great ways to order a cake, whether you’re looking for something local or want to ship it right to your doorstep:

| Option | What it offers | How to order | Best for |
|--------|----------------|--------------|----------|
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, custom‑made cakes, often with in‑store pickup or local delivery | Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Yelp, call or visit the bakery’s website | If you want a personal touch, support a local business, or need a cake within a few hours |
| **Online cake marketplaces** | Curated selection from many bakers, nationwide shipping, often same‑day delivery in major cities | Browse sites like **Goldbelly**, **Bakeology**, or **Cake Delivery**; choose a cake, add to cart, checkout | If you want a unique, artisanal cake shipped to you or someone else |
| **Major grocery chains** | Ready‑made cakes, seasonal specials, sometimes custom orders | Check the bakery section of stores like **Whole Foods**, **Trader Joe’s**, or **Walmart**; order online for pickup or delivery | If you need a quick, budget‑friendly option |
| **Specialty dessert shops** | Gourmet cakes, themed designs, often with photo‑ready packaging | Look up local dessert shops (e.g., **The Sweet Spot**, **Cake Couture**) and place an order via their website or phone | For a show‑stopping centerpiece or a themed party |
| **Subscription services** | Monthly cake deliveries, seasonal flavors | Sign up for services like **The Cake Club** or **Baker’s Dozen** | If you love trying new cakes regularly |
| **DIY kits** | All ingredients and instructions delivered | Order kits from sites like **Bakeology** or **Amazon** | If you enjoy baking at home but want a professional result |

### Quick Tips
1. **Check delivery times** – Some sites offer same‑day delivery in major metro areas, but others may take a few days.
2. **Read reviews** – Especially for online marketplaces; look for photos and customer feedback.
3. **Ask about customization** – If you have a theme, dietary restriction, or special message, confirm the baker can accommodate.
4. **Plan ahead for holidays** – Popular cakes (e.g., Christmas, Valentine’s) can book up weeks in advance.

If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up specific bakeries or delivery options that are right in your area!
